data.name: Infinity Fall
data.detailed_description:
Immerse yourself in the starship Aphelion's vast and unforgiving underbelly. You are Doctor Rupert Grouch, hounded by his own creation, DAVE. Survive time-based, combat and stealth trials, all in zero gravity. An experience uniquely suited to and built for VR.

Key Features:

- Battle or outwit an army of highly organized robots in a fully three-dimensional world. Enemies use squad-based tactics and patrol in formation. Four different enemy types, ranging from the lowly Quad-Drone to the fearsome Sentinel.

- Hone your zero gravity movement skills in challenging time trials.

- A beautiful and immersive soundtrack by trance artist Imphenzia.

- Low-nausea; generated about the same level of nausea as Google Earth VR in playtesters.

- A 3 hour campaign filled with varied challenges.

- Play at your skill level. Easy, medium, and hard difficulties.

- Currently Vive-only, Rift support coming when more than 1,000 copies are sold, update will also include a set of challenge maps.

Trailer Music: Beethoven's Coriolan Overture, performed by the Czech National Symphony Orchestra, Public Domain Mark 1.0

reviews.review:
I have yet to play Lone Echo or Echo Arena. I do own Lone Echo but I just haven't gotten around to it, but I've seen enough gameplay videos of it to get a feel for how the movement in the game is done. When the developer of Infinity Fall emailed me about his game that I had never heard of, I got really excited when I saw the initial trailer of it on its Steam Store page. As with all of the Steam keys that I've accepted, I had no requirements or restrictions as to what I could say. You can hear them in the video, but it is long, so I'll list below the things that I like but also disliked about the game, as well as the things I think would be great if added.

I love the feeling of floating in space. Launching myself out into a large room as fast as I can in order to be a harder to hit target, all while I shoot at enemy AI robots, it's a very badass feeling. Even when the game slows down and you grab onto your cover and move yourself around it is very cool feeling. I also like the levels change up between deaths so that you still have to be on your toes and you can't just memorize things through multiple deaths. The visuals and the music both gave me a System Shock vibe which meshed well with the evil, rouge AI story.

For the negatives and things that I think are missing from the game, I'll just paste what I typed in an email to the developer:

"Options menu, more things that we can change. Audio volumes with music as a separate option. In the video, so start out talking really loud and that's to make up for the music being so loud (on a side note, I really like the music in this. Has a cool techno vibe). Additional things for visuals would be nice, like super sampling and being able to disable bloom.

Controls, sort of an extension of the options menu, it would be nice to change different bindings. For me personally, it would feel more natural if I used the grip buttons for grabbing onto surfaces and such, rather than the touchpad, so it would be nice to toggle between those to choices.

As for the gameplay, I like that the hands simply moving into objects can push the player back from those objects, rather than the hand just clipping through the object, but I think it would be really, really cool if swiping out hands across a surface while we are already gliding through the air didn't stop us right there. It's a little hard to describe this, so I'll just link to a clip from the fantastic film Event Horizon. If you've never seen it and don't like blood, then I apologize for parts of this clip, but it's the closest thing to what I'm thinking of. My links should take you right to the parts I'm referring to, [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3LEa0FN1bf8&feature=youtu.be&t=9s]HERE[/url] at the 0:09 mark, [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3LEa0FN1bf8&feature=youtu.be&t=36s]HERE[/url] at the 0:36 mark, and [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3LEa0FN1bf8&feature=youtu.be&t=1m3s]HERE[/url] at the 1:03 mark, as well as a few other times, you can see how the character is keeping his momentum going by paddling with his hands. This would keep the pacing of the combat. Not sure exactly how you would do it, maybe require your hands to be moving a certain speed against a surface and the physics take in account your previous velocity and the force and direction of your hand.

I mentioned in the video at one point the ability to have very small jet packs on your wrists. There was a lot of times I would have liked them for when I launched myself but was slightly off on my direction and a little push could have set me right on my course, but also, there were multiple times that I pushed off into space but at such a slow speed that I just had to wait a while until I got close enough to grab something.

Finally, it would be nice to be able to bring up a menu without having to leave the current session. Something to pause the game in case you must take off the Vive or you just need to adjust a setting."

The developer reply favorably to my email. A future patch will likely include the visual and audio additions as well as the option to toggle between controller inputs for grabbing objects/walls. He even liked the idea of the wrist mounted propulsion, so hopefully something can come about from that. I also found out that the developer is still busy in school, which is crazy to think that this was made by someone still in that stage of their craft. Very impressive.
